spec.claim_summary: Long when 8-day EMA crosses above 21-day EMA, exit if price crosses the 21-day EMA with a maximum hold of 6 days.

claimed.other: 6 positions were taken in 10 months (304 days), an average of one every 51 days; rules produced much more profit than loss

assumptions: Direction assumed long: bullish 8 EMA crossing above 21 EMA, as typical EMA-cross setup.
Entry assumed at the bullish cross bar close; no additional trigger stated for the 6-day monitor window.
'Monitor for a maximum of 6 days' interpreted as max_hold_bars 6.
'Stop loss just the other side of the 21 day EMA and adjust daily' is a dynamic EMA stop; schema has no EMA stop so exit condition close crossing below 21 EMA is used as closest testable core.
NOT EXPRESSIBLE: dynamic stop-loss just beyond the 21-day EMA adjusted daily; replaced by fixed exit condition.
Timeframe 1d taken from page chart timeframe, not claimant words.

evidence.quote: If price crosses the 21 day EMA , your setup has failed
monitor for a maximum of 6 days
Set stop loss just the other side of the 21 day EMA
6 positions were taken in 10 months (304 days), an average of one every 51 days

audit_majors: entry[0]: Claim says 'Wait for the cross, then monitor for a maximum of 6 days' - entry is to occur sometime in a 6-day window after the cross, not at the cross bar. Spec enters immediately on the cross and has no delayed trigger condition.

max_hold_bars: 'monitor for a maximum of 6 days' is a pre-entry waiting/monitoring window, not a maximum position holding period. Spec encodes it as max_hold_bars 6, inventing an exit that claimant did not state and omitting the actual waiting-window condition.
direction: Claim says '8 day and 21 day EMAs cross' with no long-only qualifier. Spec restricts to long / crosses_above only, omitting the opposite cross direction.
